source.snippet: Github decided to disable all Github Actions (including self-hosted runners) access for our open source org for some unknown reason... the issue appeared to be some drive-by contributors who weren't org members being flagged for using Actions to do crypto-mining. As the org isn't technically in our corporate account, Github support has been unhelpful. (7 points, 2026-06-22)

problem_statement: Open-source GitHub organizations are having all CI/CD (GitHub Actions, including self-hosted runners) silently disabled due to abuse by drive-by contributors, with no clear remediation path or responsive support from GitHub.
target_segment: Maintainers of active open-source GitHub organizations, particularly those at companies that rely on CI for security-critical or infrastructure projects.
notes: Buyer signal: org maintainers who work for companies with paid GitHub corporate accounts — they have budget. The pain is both technical (broken CI) and political (no support escalation path). Opportunity: a lightweight contributor-vetting / PR-risk-scoring service that detects abuse-prone drive-by contributors before they trigger platform bans. Could be sold as a GitHub App subscription to org admins at $20–50/mo. Adjacent: CI abuse insurance / monitoring.
